usage.examples:
# AI label examples

Mark generated content beside the text it describes.

```html
<header>Weekly summary <ki-ai-label></ki-ai-label></header>
```

Give people a short provenance explanation when they need to assess a result.
The model and generation time are optional.

```html
<ki-ai-label
  explanation="Written from the incident reports of the last 30 days."
  model="Standard"
  generated-at="2026-11-19T10:32"
></ki-ai-label>
```

Use the input's `end` slot to announce the provenance with the field
description. Keep the original in application state and restore it on
`ki-revert`.

```html
<ki-input id="subject" label="Subject" value="Incident summary">
  <ki-ai-label
    slot="end"
    explanation="Suggested from the incident reports."
    revertible
  ></ki-ai-label>
</ki-input>

<script type="module">
  const field = document.querySelector('#subject');
  const label = field.querySelector('ki-ai-label');
  const original = 'Weekly summary';

  label.addEventListener('ki-revert', () => {
    field.value = original;
    label.remove();
    field.focus();
  });
</script>
```

components.docs: A persistent inline status message with token-backed tone semantics.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
show a persistent inline message about the state of a page or
section, such as a failed save, completed operation, or service notice, that
remains until the condition is resolved or the person dismisses it. Express
severity with `tone`, never custom styling.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
transient confirmations that expire on their own belong to
`ki-toast`, raised into a `ki-toaster`; tiny status descriptors attached to
another element belong to `ki-badge`; blocking decisions belong to
`ki-dialog`; inline field-level validation belongs to the form control.

Assistive technology note: alerts that must be announced should be inserted
dynamically, or re-shown by clearing `dismissed`; alerts present at initial
page load are exposed with their role but platform announcement is not
guaranteed.

Every non-neutral alert should carry an icon: in the onmars theme the tone
is drawn on the icon alone.

carries meaning the heading and message lack. When to use: give every

message.

person cannot skip belongs in `ki-dialog`.

usage.examples:
`tone` sets the token-backed colors and the live-region urgency — `danger` and `warning` expose `role="alert"`, every other value `role="status"`:

```html
<ki-alert tone="success">Your changes were saved.</ki-alert>
<ki-alert tone="danger">Payment failed. Update your billing details.</ki-alert>
```

An optional `heading` adds emphasized text inside the live region; it is a `strong` element, never a document heading:

```html
<ki-alert tone="warning" heading="Storage almost full">
  You are using 92% of your plan.
</ki-alert>
```

`dismissible` renders the alert's only tab stop; user dismissal reflects `dismissed` and fires a composed `ki-dismiss` (programmatic `dismissed` writes stay silent, and clearing the attribute re-shows the alert):

```html
<ki-alert tone="danger" heading="Save failed" dismissible>
  Your changes could not be saved. Retry or copy your work elsewhere.
</ki-alert>
```

`dismiss-label` overrides the dismiss button's accessible name — the default `Dismiss` is the component's only built-in user-visible string, so localize it whenever the document language is not English:

```html
<ki-alert lang="es" tone="info" dismissible dismiss-label="Descartar">
  Mantenimiento programado el sábado desde las 02:00 UTC.
</ki-alert>
```

The `icon` slot takes a decorative glyph, drawn in the tone's colors in a round frame at the top of the card; give every non-neutral alert one, since that is where the tone shows. The `actions` slot takes the responses to the message as `size="sm"` buttons, in a row after the message and outside the live region. An action never dismisses the alert by itself: set `dismissed` when it should go, and focus moves on to the next control:

```html
<ki-alert tone="warning" heading="Session ending" dismissible>
  <svg slot="icon" viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true">
    <path fill="currentColor" d="M10 2a8 8 0 1 0 0 16 8 8 0 0 0 0-16Zm.75 4v4.5h-1.5V6h1.5Zm-.75 8.25a1 1 0 1 1 0-2 1 1 0 0 1 0 2Z" />
  </svg>
  Your session expires in one minute. Choose Stay signed in to keep working.
  <ki-button slot="actions" type="button" variant="secondary" size="sm">Sign out</ki-button>
  <ki-button slot="actions" type="button" variant="primary" size="sm">Stay signed in</ki-button>
</ki-alert>
```

props.name: dismissLabel
props.docs:
Accessible name for the dismiss button. Override for localization; the
default English string is the component's only built-in user-visible text.

When to use: provide a localized action name whenever the document language
is not English.
When NOT to use: do not put the alert message here; use the default slot.

docsTags.text: 'Dismiss'

props.name: dismissed
props.docs:
Reflected dismissed state. User dismissal sets it; applications may also
set or clear it. While true, the host remains in the document but renders no
alert subtree and leaves the accessibility tree. Clearing it re-shows the
alert and creates a dynamic live-region appearance.

When to use: persist or restore acknowledgement state from application
data.
When NOT to use: do not listen for programmatic changes as dismissal
events; `ki-dismiss` is only for user activation.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: false

props.name: dismissible
props.docs:
Renders one native dismiss button when true. The button sits outside the
live-region boundary, so its accessible name is not announced as part of
the alert message. When false, the alert adds no tab stop.

When to use: allow a person to acknowledge and clear a persistent message.
When NOT to use: do not use dismissible for auto-expiring messages; those
belong to `ki-toast`.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: false

props.name: heading
props.docs:
Optional emphasized text rendered before the message inside the live
region. Empty strings render no heading. The heading is a `strong`
element, not a document heading, so it never changes page outline.

When to use: add a short label when it helps identify the status message.
When NOT to use: do not use heading for page structure; use a real heading
outside the alert when the document needs one.

props.name: tone
props.docs:
Semantic intent for visual styling and live-region urgency. `danger` and
`warning` expose `role="alert"`; `neutral`, `success`, `info`, absent, and
unrecognized values expose `role="status"`. Unknown values keep rendering
and fall back to the neutral token matrix by CSS construction.

When to use: choose the tone that describes the page or section state.
When NOT to use: do not use tone for layout, density, or filled-vs-outlined
styling; those are token/theme decisions.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: 'neutral'

events.docs:
Fired once after the user dismisses the alert — emitted after the alert is
hidden and focus has been handed to the next control. `detail` is `null`
and the event is not cancelable (the alert is already gone when it runs).
When to use: record acknowledgement, or advance an application flow after a
user closes the alert.
When NOT to use: do not treat it as a veto point, and do not expect it for
programmatic `dismissed` changes — it fires only for user activation.

A static identity visual that shows a person or entity at a glance through
a fallback chain: portrait, then initials, then a built-in generic figure.

docsTags.name: whenToUse

a compact identity visual for a person or entity — a comment
author, a contact list item, a project member. Set `label` whenever the
avatar is the only carrier of the identity (no adjacent visible name);
compose several into `ki-avatar-group` for a compact "who is involved"
stack with overflow.

(plain `img`), or unlabeled when no adjacent text names the identity.

props.docs:
Initials rendered verbatim as the second fallback step — never derived
from the label, never truncated (FR-003). Catalog guidance: one to two
characters. With a label present the initials are presentational;
assistive technology receives the label alone.

Accessible name for the identity ("Ana García"). With a label the avatar

components.docs:
A token-styled companion container that stacks `ki-avatar` children as one
overlapping row with a configurable visible cap and a static "+N" overflow
counter.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
a compact "who is involved" stack — the members of a shared
document, project card or event row — where space deserves only the first
few identities and an exact "+N" counter accounts for the rest.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
as a member picker or expandable overflow (future interactive
grouping — the counter is static text, never a button), for a single
identity (use `ki-avatar` alone), or with children other than `ki-avatar`
(foreign markup is unsupported and not repaired, 016 precedent).

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text:
- `ki-avatar` members, stacked in source order. Members beyond the
visible cap are neither rendered nor exposed to assistive technology.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: group - The stack row containing the members and the counter.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: counter - The static "+N" overflow text trailing the stack.

usage.examples:
`max` caps the visible stack; members beyond the cap are neither rendered nor exposed to assistive technology, and a static "+N" counter accounts exactly for the hidden rest:

```html
<ki-avatar-group max="3">
  <ki-avatar label="Ana García" initials="AG"></ki-avatar>
  <ki-avatar label="Sam Bel" initials="SB"></ki-avatar>
  <ki-avatar label="Iris Toma" initials="IT"></ki-avatar>
  <ki-avatar label="Leo Duarte" initials="LD"></ki-avatar>
  <ki-avatar label="Mia Chen" initials="MC"></ki-avatar>
</ki-avatar-group>
<!-- renders Ana, Sam and Iris, then "+2" -->
```

Without `max` — or with a cap that is not a positive whole number — every member renders and no counter appears (never "+0"):

```html
<ki-avatar-group>
  <ki-avatar label="Ana García" initials="AG"></ki-avatar>
  <ki-avatar label="Sam Bel" initials="SB"></ki-avatar>
</ki-avatar-group>
```

The group's `size` governs every visible member and the counter, overriding member-declared sizes so the stack stays uniform:

```html
<ki-avatar-group size="sm" max="2">
  <ki-avatar label="Ana García" initials="AG" size="xl"></ki-avatar>
  <ki-avatar label="Sam Bel" initials="SB"></ki-avatar>
  <ki-avatar label="Iris Toma" initials="IT"></ki-avatar>
</ki-avatar-group>
```

props.name: max
props.docs:
Visible cap for the member stack. When the member count exceeds it, the
first `max` members render followed by a "+N" counter accounting exactly
for the hidden rest. Without it — or when it is not a positive whole
number — every member renders and no counter appears; malformed
agent-generated markup never breaks the page (FR-009, S14, S15).

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: undefined

props.name: size
props.docs:
Size step governing the metrics of every visible member and the counter
(avatar vocabulary, FR-010). Member-declared sizes are overridden inside
a group so the stack stays uniform (S6). An unrecognized value matches
no style selector, so the group keeps the default medium metrics
(FR-007).

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: 'md'

only reinforces the text, it never replaces it.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
feedback that must be announced (that is
ki-alert's job — the badge has no live region), an interactive
chip, filter or button, empty content (the label IS the meaning), or a
notification-counter overlay (use ki-counter).

usage.examples:
The slotted label is the sole carrier of meaning; `tone` only reinforces it with the `--ki-badge-{tone}-*` token colors, and an unrecognized value keeps the neutral appearance:

```html
<ki-badge>Draft</ki-badge>
<ki-badge tone="info">Beta</ki-badge>
<ki-badge tone="success">Active</ki-badge>
<ki-badge tone="warning">Trial ends soon</ki-badge>
<ki-badge tone="danger">Suspended</ki-badge>
```

`size` selects the metric scale (`sm` or `md`, default `md`):

```html
<ki-badge tone="success" size="sm">Synced</ki-badge>
```

A typical placement — trailing status on a list entry:

```html
<ki-list>
  <ki-list-item>
    Production deploy
    <ki-badge slot="end" tone="success">Healthy</ki-badge>
  </ki-list-item>
</ki-list>
```

usage.examples:
## Show the path to the current page

```html
<ki-breadcrumb label="Project path">
  <ki-breadcrumb-item href="/workspace">Workspace</ki-breadcrumb-item>
  <ki-breadcrumb-item href="/workspace/projects">Projects</ki-breadcrumb-item>
  <ki-breadcrumb-item current>Settings</ki-breadcrumb-item>
</ki-breadcrumb>
```

## Collapse middle levels

```html
<ki-breadcrumb label="Release path" max-items="4">
  <ki-breadcrumb-item href="/workspace">Workspace</ki-breadcrumb-item>
  <ki-breadcrumb-item href="/projects">Projects</ki-breadcrumb-item>
  <ki-breadcrumb-item href="/projects/kimen">Kimen</ki-breadcrumb-item>
  <ki-breadcrumb-item href="/projects/kimen/packages">Packages</ki-breadcrumb-item>
  <ki-breadcrumb-item href="/projects/kimen/releases">Releases</ki-breadcrumb-item>
  <ki-breadcrumb-item current>v2.4.0</ki-breadcrumb-item>
</ki-breadcrumb>
```

In this example the overflow has three levels. The trail shows Workspace,
the overflow button, Releases, and v2.4.0.

## Render a guarded breadcrumb

Put breadcrumb items in the default slot and supply plain-text item labels.
The surface's URL policy applies to each destination. Native links have no
custom action binding.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "root": {
    "component": "ki-breadcrumb",
    "props": { "label": "Project path" },
    "slots": {
      "": [
        {
          "component": "ki-breadcrumb-item",
          "props": { "href": "/workspace" },
          "slots": { "": ["Workspace"] }
        },
        {
          "component": "ki-breadcrumb-item",
          "props": { "current": true },
          "slots": { "": ["Settings"] }
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

A form-associated checkbox for selecting independent options.

Like a native field, it answers `checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()`,
`setCustomValidity(message)`, `validity`, `validationMessage` and
`willValidate` synchronously, on the custom-elements build (not on hosts
created by the lazy loader).

later, including a "select all" parent that presents partial selection with
`indeterminate`. Always provide a visible label in the default slot.

effect, triggering an action, unlabeled/icon-only usage, or
`checked="false"` to mean unchecked. Boolean attributes use presence
semantics; omit `checked` to express unchecked.

docsTags.text:
change - Fired once after a user toggle (pointer, slotted label or Space)
commits, composed across the shadow boundary; `checked` is already current
when listeners run. When to use: react to the committed selection. When NOT
to use: do not expect it for programmatic `checked` writes, which are silent.

usage.examples:
The default slot is the visible label — the accessible name and a native activation surface; when checked, `name` and `value` pair into the submitted form data:

```html
<form>
  <ki-checkbox name="channels" value="email" checked>Email</ki-checkbox>
  <ki-checkbox name="channels" value="sms">SMS</ki-checkbox>
  <ki-button variant="primary">Save preferences</ki-button>
</form>
```

Boolean attributes use presence semantics — omit `checked` to express unchecked, never write `checked="false"`; without `value` a checked box submits `on`, and unchecked boxes contribute no form entry:

```html
<ki-checkbox name="newsletter" checked>Send me the weekly digest</ki-checkbox>
```

`required` blocks submission while unchecked (the invalid appearance appears only after a blocked attempt or an invalidating toggle, never on initial render), and `disabled` removes the checkbox from keyboard reach and form data:

```html
<form>
  <ki-checkbox name="terms" required>I accept the terms of service</ki-checkbox>
  <ki-checkbox name="fax" disabled>Notify me by fax</ki-checkbox>
  <ki-button variant="primary">Create account</ki-button>
</form>
```

`indeterminate` presents the mixed state of a "select all" parent — presentation-only, exposed to assistive technology as mixed, cleared by any user toggle, and never submitted (model data stays binary through `checked`):

```html
<ki-checkbox indeterminate>Select all rows</ki-checkbox>
```

usage.examples:
# Checkbox group examples

## Submit several selections

```html
<form id="settings">
  <ki-checkbox-group
    id="regions"
    label="Regions"
    name="regions"
    min="1"
    help-text="Choose the regions you serve."
    error-text="Choose at least one region."
  >
    <ki-checkbox value="eu" checked>Europe</ki-checkbox>
    <ki-checkbox value="am">Americas</ki-checkbox>
    <ki-checkbox value="apac">Asia-Pacific</ki-checkbox>
  </ki-checkbox-group>
  <button type="submit">Save regions</button>
</form>
```

Reading `new FormData(form).getAll('regions')` returns each checked value
in option order. Keep individual option labels visible and give each option
a distinct value when you need to select it independently from JavaScript.

## Read and update selection

```js
import { defineCustomElement as defineCheckbox } from '@kimen/elements/ki-checkbox';
import { defineCustomElement as defineCheckboxGroup } from '@kimen/elements/ki-checkbox-group';

defineCheckbox();
defineCheckboxGroup();

const group = document.querySelector('#regions');
group.value = ['eu', 'apac'];

group.addEventListener('ki-change', (event) => {
  const selectedRegions = event.detail.value;
  console.log(selectedRegions);
});
```

## Horizontal choices

```html
<ki-checkbox-group label="Notifications" orientation="horizontal">
  <ki-checkbox value="mentions">Mentions</ki-checkbox>
  <ki-checkbox value="reviews">Review requests</ki-checkbox>
</ki-checkbox-group>
```

usage.examples:
# Chip examples

Use a filter group for independent toggles. Read `ki-change.detail.selected` to
update the results. The chip's `value` identifies the filter.

```html
<ki-chip-group label="Team" type="filter">
  <ki-chip value="design" selected>Design</ki-chip>
  <ki-chip value="eng">Engineering</ki-chip>
</ki-chip-group>
```

Use an input group for picked values. Link the entry field by ID so focus
returns to it after the last chip. Listen to `ki-remove` to update your
collection. If a framework owns these nodes, cancel the event and let it
apply the DOM change, then focus the next chip or the linked field.

```html
<ki-chip-group label="Recipients" type="input" focus-target="recipient">
  <ki-chip value="ana" removable>
    <ki-avatar slot="start" size="xxs" initials="AG" label="Ana García"></ki-avatar>
    Ana García
  </ki-chip>
  <ki-chip value="luis" removable>Luis</ki-chip>
</ki-chip-group>
<input id="recipient" aria-label="Add recipient">
```

Use assist for a contextual action. Handle `ki-activate` in application code.

```html
<ki-chip type="assist" value="calendar">
  <svg slot="start" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor">
    <rect x="3" y="5" width="18" height="16" rx="2"/>
    <path d="M3 10h18M8 2v6m8-6v6"/>
  </svg>
  Add to calendar
</ki-chip>
```

# ki-code-block examples

Display a TypeScript snippet with line numbers and a highlighted line.

```html
<ki-code-block language="ts" filename="main.ts" line-numbers highlight="2">// Load the current sample.

brackets so they remain part of the source.

<ki-code-block language="html" filename="example.html" wrap copyable="false"><p>Hello</p></ki-code-block>

usage.examples:
## Search people

When importing custom elements individually, register both
`@kimen/elements/ki-combobox` and `@kimen/elements/ki-option`.

```html
<ki-combobox label="Assignee" name="assignee" placeholder="Search people" required>
  <ki-option value="ana" description="ana@example.com">Ana Ruiz</ki-option>
  <ki-option value="juan" description="juan@example.com">Juan Antón</ki-option>
</ki-combobox>
```

## Pick or create multiple labels

```html
<ki-combobox label="Labels" name="labels" multiple allow-custom value='["bug","search"]'>
  <ki-option>bug</ki-option>
  <ki-option>search</ki-option>
  <ki-option>documentation</ki-option>
</ki-combobox>
```

Assign an array to the JavaScript `value` property to set multiple selections.
Use a JSON array string in HTML or neutral catalog specs. Each selection
submits under the same form name. Read them all with `FormData.getAll`.

## Request server results

Set `filter="none"` to display the options supplied by your application.
Listen for `ki-input` and use `event.detail.value` as the query. Set `loading`
while fetching, replace the field's `ki-option` children with the latest
results, and clear `loading`. Use `change` to respond to a committed selection.

usage.examples:
# Using ki-fab

Use one FAB for the primary action of a screen. Give it a localized `label`
in every layout. Import each Lucide glyph before mounting a FAB that names it.
Use the native `click` event to call your application's action handler.

```js
import '@kimen/elements/icons/pencil';
import { defineCustomElement } from '@kimen/elements/ki-fab';

defineCustomElement();

document.querySelector('#compose')?.addEventListener('click', openComposer);
```

```html
<ki-fab id="compose" label="Compose" icon-name="pencil"></ki-fab>
```

Use `href` when activation takes the user to a destination. To supply a custom
glyph, use the `icon` slot with decorative, noninteractive content.

```html
<ki-fab label="New project" href="/projects/new" variant="primary" extended>
  <svg slot="icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false">
    <path d="M5 12h14M12 5v14"></path>
  </svg>
</ki-fab>
```

Place a fixed FAB after the main content so its tab stop follows the page's
controls. Reserve bottom space so the last item can scroll above it. Set
`--ki-fab-mobile-nav-block-size` to the height of the fixed navigation when
present, excluding the safe area.

```html
<main class="compose-page">
  <!-- Page content -->
</main>
<ki-fab label="Compose" icon-name="pencil" position="fixed" extended collapse-on-scroll></ki-fab>
```

```css
:root {
  --ki-fab-mobile-nav-block-size: var(--app-mobile-nav-height, 0px);
  --compose-clearance: calc(
    var(--ki-fab-size) + 2 * var(--ki-fab-offset) +
      var(--ki-fab-mobile-nav-block-size) + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)
  );
  scroll-padding-block-end: var(--compose-clearance);
}

.compose-page {
  padding-block-end: var(--compose-clearance);
}
```

The clearance above uses the default `md` size. Adjust it for a larger FAB
and use the actual expanded height if the label wraps. The label hides as the
user scrolls down the document and reappears on upward scroll. The native
control retains its accessible name and focus.

usage.examples:
The default slot holds exactly one decorative icon; the mandatory `label` is the accessible name — the slot never contributes to it:

```html
<ki-icon-button label="Close">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M6 6l12 12M18 6L6 18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" /></svg>
</ki-icon-button>
```

Visual hierarchy comes from `variant` (default `secondary`). In the original momentary variants, `tone` (default `neutral`) carries semantic intent such as success or danger.

```html
<ki-icon-button variant="primary" label="Play">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M8 5v14l11-7z" fill="currentColor" /></svg>
</ki-icon-button>
<ki-icon-button variant="ghost" tone="danger" label="Delete row">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M6 7h12M9 7V5h6v2m-8 0l1 12h8l1-12" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" fill="none" /></svg>
</ki-icon-button>
```

Add `toggle` for an action such as Bookmark that stays pressed until the next activation. `variant="outline"` uses an outline at rest and a fill when selected. Give the pressed version a decorative icon in the `selected` slot.

```html
<ki-icon-button toggle variant="outline" label="Bookmark">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" aria-hidden="true">
    <path d="M6 3h12v18l-6-4-6 4z" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" />
  </svg>
  <svg slot="selected" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor" aria-hidden="true">
    <path d="M6 3h12v18l-6-4-6 4z" />
  </svg>
</ki-icon-button>
```

With an empty `selected` slot, the default inline SVG takes a `currentColor` fill while pressed. Let its paths inherit `fill`. Keep `label` the same in both states. Activating the control emits `ki-change` with `{ selected }`. Set the `selected` attribute for the initial state or write the property to update it silently.

Sizes run `xs` (24px, exactly the WCAG 2.2 pointer-target floor) through `xl`, default `md`; each pairs a square box with its own icon size:

```html
<ki-icon-button size="xs" label="Clear">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M6 6l12 12M18 6L6 18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" /></svg>
</ki-icon-button>
<ki-icon-button size="xl" variant="primary" label="Record">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="6" fill="currentColor" /></svg>
</ki-icon-button>
```

Pair with `ki-tooltip` for sighted discoverability: the tooltip's `label` becomes the accessible description while the icon button's `label` stays the accessible name:

```html
<ki-tooltip label="Closes the dialog">
  <ki-icon-button label="Close">
    <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M6 6l12 12M18 6L6 18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" /></svg>
  </ki-icon-button>
</ki-tooltip>
```

An icon button in the dialog footer can dismiss it by ID. The dialog must be
in the same document or shadow root as the icon button.

```html

</ki-icon-button>
```

While the action it started is in progress, set `loading` instead of `disabled`: the icon button keeps its size, its focus and its `label`, ignores further activation, draws a spinner in place of the icon and announces `loading-label` (default "Loading") as a polite status message:

```html
<ki-icon-button label="Refresh" loading loading-label="Refreshing">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M4 12a8 8 0 0 1 14-5l2 2M20 12a8 8 0 0 1-14 5l-2-2" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" fill="none" /></svg>
</ki-icon-button>
```

components.docs:
A non-interactive page-position indicator: one dot per position of a
bounded sequence, exactly one highlighted as current.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
show the current position within a bounded, sequential set of
peer views whose navigation lives elsewhere: carousel slides, unlabeled
onboarding steps, gallery pages. Wire `count` and `current` (1-based) to
the sequence the consumer renders and give it a `label` (required
authoring: assistive technology reads one graphic named
"<label>, <current> / <count>"). Below two positions an indicator carries
no information.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
section navigation (ki-tabs), task completion or loading
(ki-progress), labeled step flows (a stepper is a separate roadmap item),
interactive pagination (a future feature — the indicator takes no focus
and no input; navigation belongs to the composing carousel's own
controls), or conveying quantity without a current position. Position
changes are never announced by the indicator itself (no live region): the
composing carousel owns announcements.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: indicator - The row container: layout and the token-driven gap.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: dot - Every dot: size, shape and color.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: dot-current - Additionally on the current dot: the highlight treatment.

usage.examples:
Two integers determine everything — one dot per `count` position with the 1-based `current` highlighted — and `label` names the sequence (the exposed name reads "<label>, <current> / <count>"):

```html
<ki-indicator label="Slide position" count="5" current="2"></ki-indicator>
```

Malformed declarations never break the row: `current` above `count` clamps to the last position, a non-numeric one falls back to the first, and an invalid `count` renders zero dots (an authoring mistake, not an error state):

```html
<ki-indicator label="Slide position" count="5" current="9"></ki-indicator>
<!-- fifth dot current -->
```

Drive it from the composing carousel by updating `current` (1-based); the highlight and exposed text follow immediately, and the indicator never announces changes (no live region) — announcements belong to the carousel:

```html
<ki-indicator id="gallery-position" label="Photo position" count="4" current="1"></ki-indicator>

<script type="module">
  const indicator = document.getElementById('gallery-position');
  indicator.current = 3;
</script>
```

props.name: count
props.docs:
Number of positions (non-negative integer): one dot renders per
position, in position order. A missing, non-numeric or negative value
renders zero dots — an authoring mistake by catalog guidance, never an
error state or a rendering failure (FR-002; empty ki-list precedent).
At most 20 positions render, and the catalog accepts no more: the
indicator serves a short sequence of peer views, 20 dots are the longest
row that fits a 320 CSS px viewport (the WCAG reflow width) in both
shipped themes, and one dot renders per position, so the bound also caps
the work a single node can demand. A larger value renders 20.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: undefined

props.name: current
props.docs:
The current position, 1-based to match the exposed position text
("2 / 5"). Exactly one dot presents the current appearance whenever
`count` >= 1: values above `count` clamp to the last position, values
below 1 and non-numeric values fall back to the first (FR-003). Updates
re-render in place — the highlight and the exposed text follow
immediately, re-applying the normalization (FR-004). The catalog accepts
1 to 20, the positions a bounded `count` can have.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: undefined

props.name: label
props.docs:
Accessible name of the sequence ("Slide position"). The exposed name
combines it with the wordless numeric position —
"<label>, <current> / <count>" — on a single non-interactive graphic;
without a label the name degrades to the bare position text (documented
as required authoring, FR-005). The label is never rendered visually
and position changes are never announced (no live region, FR-006).

A token-styled single-line text field with native input semantics.

Like a native field, it answers `checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()`,
`setCustomValidity(message)`, `validity`, `validationMessage` and
`willValidate` synchronously, on the custom-elements build (not on hosts
created by the lazy loader).

docsTags.name: whenToUse

collect one line of free text from a person, always with a
visible `label`; choose the `type` and `autocomplete` that match the entry
purpose.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
multiline text, predefined choices, boolean state, numeric
stepper entry, or placeholder-only labeling.

A directly slotted AI label also describes the field as suggested by AI.

Use for one-field forms such as search or subscribe. Place a named
`ki-button size="sm" type="submit"` here, or wire a labeled
`ki-icon-button size="sm"` to request form submission. The action has its own tab
stop. Use the end slot for clear or reveal controls.

after the person answered or submitted; a polite live region, starting with a

part of the accessible name; rendered only while a hint is set.

docsTags.text:
change - Fired when the user commits an edited value (native text-field
timing, such as on blur), composed across the shadow boundary; `value` is
already current when listeners run. When to use: react to a committed
value. When NOT to use: do not use it for per-keystroke updates; the native
`input` event carries those.

usage.examples:
A labeled field participating in native form submission (`label` is mandatory; it is the accessible name):

```html
<form>
  <ki-input label="Work email" name="email" type="email" required></ki-input>
  <ki-button variant="primary">Subscribe</ki-button>
</form>
```

Place a one-field form's only submit action inside the field.

```html
<form role="search">
  <ki-input type="search" name="q" label="Search docs" placeholder="Components, tokens…">
    <ki-button slot="action" size="sm" variant="secondary" type="submit">Search</ki-button>
  </ki-input>
</form>
```

The action has a separate tab stop. Enter in the entry also submits the form.
For an icon-only action, give `ki-icon-button size="sm"` a `label` and call
`form.requestSubmit()` from its click handler.

Read-only and disabled are distinct states — read-only stays focusable and is submitted, disabled is neither:

```html
<ki-input label="Plan" value="Pro" readonly></ki-input>
<ki-input label="Legacy ID" value="A-1042" disabled></ki-input>
```

Without it the browser's own message shows, in the browser's language. An
error set with `setCustomValidity` outranks it.
When NOT to use: do not use it for server-side or cross-field errors; call
`setCustomValidity` for those.

props.name: helpText
props.docs:
One line of help under the field, read with it as its description: the
format expected, or why the answer is asked. While an error shows, the

When NOT to use: do not repeat the label, and do not use it for error
messages; use `error-text`.

props.name: label
props.docs:
Visible label rendered next to the entry area and used as the accessible

When NOT to use: never use `placeholder` as a label substitute.

props.name: labelHint
props.docs:
Short text shown after the label and read with it as part of the field's
name, so people know before submitting whether to answer: "(optional)" on

other way round, in the page's own language. It changes no validation;
set `required` for that, and keep the two consistent.
When NOT to use: do not put instructions or formats in it (use
`help-text`), errors (use `error-text`), or a repeat of the label.

When NOT to use: use `disabled` when the value must be unavailable and

props.docs:

When NOT to use: do not use required on optional fields.

props.name: size
props.docs:
Token-backed field size (`--ki-input-{size}-*` tokens): the field box is
24, 32, 40, 48 or 56px tall in onmars, with its padding, radius, text and
icon box; the label and help text follow in three steps. An unrecognized
value matches no style rule and keeps the medium metrics.
When to use: match the size of the buttons and fields around it.
When NOT to use: do not pick a smaller size to fit a dense region or a
larger one for touch; declare `data-ki-density` on the region instead,
which composes with every size.

docsTags.text: 'md'

props.docs:

props.name: value

Live text value. The attribute declares the initial default; the property
is the current value and programmatic assignments are silent.

attribute's current value.

and `change` (both re-dispatched composed across the shadow boundary).

# When to use Menu

Use Menu for commands on the same object, account actions, split buttons and
overflow actions. Keep destructive actions at the end after a divider. Pick
a select for a form value, links for navigation, or a dialog or page for
long action lists.

catalog action on the menu's declared `ki-select` event. Application DOM
listeners can read the selected item's `value` and optional `checked` from
the event detail.

# ki-note usage

Place one or two lines of static context beside a control or inside a card.
Use `ki-alert` for results that need announcing, Toast for transient
confirmations and the field's `help-text` for field guidance.

```html
<ki-note>Only workspace owners can change billing details.</ki-note>
<ki-note tone="warning" size="sm">Changing the slug breaks existing links.</ki-note>
<ki-note tone="info" icon="false">This link is visible to everyone in the workspace.</ki-note>
```

## Decorative icon replacement

```html
<ki-note tone="info">
  <svg slot="icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2">
    <path d="M12 3v18M3 12h18"></path>
  </svg>
  Adding a billing contact gives them access to invoices.
</ki-note>
```

The words convey the message by themselves. The decorative icon is hidden
from assistive technology and adds no tab stop. Start warnings with the
consequence.

# ki-number-input examples

## Quantity with bounds

```html
<ki-number-input label="Seats" name="seats" value="3" min="1" max="50" steppers required></ki-number-input>
```

## Plain field with a unit

```html
<ki-number-input label="Timeout" name="timeout" value="30" unit="seconds" min="0"></ki-number-input>
```

The form submits `timeout=30`.

## Percentage with localized editing

```html
<ki-number-input
  lang="de-DE"
  label="Discount"
  name="discount"
  min="0"
  max="1"
  step="0.005"
  value="0.125"
  format='{"style":"percent","maximumFractionDigits":1}'
></ki-number-input>
```

The editor displays `12,5` while focused and formats it as a percentage on
blur. The form submits `discount=0.125`.

## Custom-elements entry point

```ts
import { defineCustomElement } from '@kimen/elements/ki-number-input';

defineCustomElement();
const discount = document.querySelector('ki-number-input[name="discount"]');
if (discount) {
  discount.format = { style: 'percent', maximumFractionDigits: 1 };
}
```

usage.examples:
An option is meaningful only inside `ki-select`: it does not paint itself — the trimmed text is the visible label the select mirrors into its popup listbox, and `value` is what the form submits:

```html
<ki-select label="Language" name="language" placeholder="Choose a language">
  <ki-option value="en">English</ki-option>
  <ki-option value="es">Spanish</ki-option>
  <ki-option value="pt">Portuguese</ki-option>
</ki-select>
```

Omitting `value` submits the trimmed option text (native `<option>` parity); `disabled` options cannot be selected, are skipped by keyboard highlight, and are exposed unavailable by the select:

```html
<ki-select label="Priority" name="priority">
  <ki-option>Low</ki-option>
  <ki-option>Medium</ki-option>
  <ki-option disabled>Urgent</ki-option>
</ki-select>
```

Never author selection on the option — assign `ki-select.value` and the first matching option is selected silently:

```html
<ki-select id="language" label="Language" name="language">
  <ki-option value="en">English</ki-option>
  <ki-option value="es">Spanish</ki-option>
</ki-select>

<script type="module">
  document.getElementById('language').value = 'es';
</script>
```

the completed fraction is known; use `indeterminate` when work is ongoing
but its duration cannot be measured, including loading-indicator use cases.
Choose `linear` in page flows and lists, and `circular` in compact or
centered placements. Always set `label` to what is progressing.

usage.examples:
A determinate task; `label` names what is progressing (without it the progressbar exposes no accessible name) and `value` is clamped to `0..max` for both presentation and ARIA:

```html
<ki-progress label="Uploading report.pdf" value="42"></ki-progress>
```

When the total is not 100, set `max`; non-finite, zero or negative totals normalize to `100`:

```html
<ki-progress label="Installing dependencies" value="3" max="8"></ki-progress>
```

Unknown-duration work sets `indeterminate` instead of a fabricated `value` (which is ignored while it is set); the motion is declared only when reduced motion is not requested:

```html
<ki-progress label="Contacting server" indeterminate></ki-progress>
```

`shape="circular"` fits compact or centered placements; unknown shape values render linear:

```html
<ki-progress label="Export progress" shape="circular" value="80"></ki-progress>
```

A machine-scannable QR code that hands a declared value — a link, a
pairing payload — from the screen to a nearby camera, encoded locally
and restyled entirely through tokens.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
hand a URL or machine-readable payload from the screen to a
nearby camera device: login pairing, tickets and passes, "continue on
mobile" links, Wi-Fi sharing. Declare `value` (encoded verbatim, always
locally) and a purpose-stating `label` ("Open onmars.dev on your phone"),
and always offer the same payload through an accessible alternative next
to the code — a visible link or copyable text — because a QR code is only
useful to someone who can point a second device's camera at the screen.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
data the person must read on this same screen (render text
or a link), one-dimensional barcodes (out of scope), anything interactive
(a QR code is not a button — pair it with a real control instead), secret
values (anyone who can photograph the screen can decode them), or as the
sole carrier of the payload (the accessible alternative is mandatory
guidance). An always-empty ki-qr and a value beyond the ~2,331-byte
capacity are authoring mistakes: both render nothing, silently.

Accessible name stating the code's purpose ("Open onmars.dev on your
phone"). The component exposes exactly one non-interactive image named
by it, falling back to the encoded value when absent (FR-005) — never
an unnamed graphic. The label is never rendered visually, and naming
the purpose is what tells assistive-technology users to look for the
accessible alternative carrying the same payload (documented catalog
guidance, FR-013).

props.name: value
props.docs:
The exact text the code encodes — the single source of the content,
encoded locally as one UTF-8 byte segment at error-correction level M
(non-ASCII text additionally carries the UTF-8 ECI designator, so real
scanners decode the declared string rather than an ISO-8859-1
misreading), so an independent decoder recovers it byte-for-byte,
including non-ASCII text (FR-001), and no network request is ever made — the value is
data, never behavior: the component never interprets, resolves,
navigates to or fetches it (FR-002). Changes re-encode in place. When
absent, empty or beyond the capacity of the densest symbol (~2,331
bytes at level M), nothing renders and nothing errors (FR-003).

usage.examples:
Each option is a `ki-radio` child of a `ki-radio-group`; the slotted text is the option's accessible name and activation surface, and `value` is what the group submits when the option is selected:

```html
<ki-radio-group label="Delivery speed" name="delivery">
  <ki-radio value="standard">Standard (3–5 days)</ki-radio>
  <ki-radio value="express">Express (1–2 days)</ki-radio>
</ki-radio-group>
```

A disabled option cannot be selected or focused, and group arrow navigation skips it:

```html
<ki-radio-group label="Plan" name="plan" value="pro">
  <ki-radio value="free">Free</ki-radio>
  <ki-radio value="pro">Pro</ki-radio>
  <ki-radio value="enterprise" disabled>Enterprise (contact sales)</ki-radio>
</ki-radio-group>
```

Selection is never authored on the option — the parent group's `value` selects the matching option:

```html
<ki-radio-group label="Theme" name="theme" value="dark">
  <ki-radio value="light">Light</ki-radio>
  <ki-radio value="dark">Dark</ki-radio>
  <ki-radio value="system">Match system</ki-radio>
</ki-radio-group>
```

on/off settings (use `ki-checkbox` or `ki-switch`), multiple selection, or

usage.examples:
The group owns the `label` (mandatory; the radiogroup's accessible name), the form `name` and the selected `value`; user selection dispatches a composed `change` event, while programmatic `value` writes stay silent:

```html
<ki-radio-group label="Delivery speed" name="delivery" value="standard">
  <ki-radio value="standard">Standard (3–5 days)</ki-radio>
  <ki-radio value="express">Express (1–2 days)</ki-radio>
  <ki-radio value="overnight">Overnight</ki-radio>
</ki-radio-group>
```

Without an initial `value` the group renders unselected and operable; `required` blocks form submission through the platform `valueMissing` validity until an option is chosen:

```html
<form>
  <ki-radio-group label="Billing cycle" name="cycle" required>
    <ki-radio value="monthly">Monthly</ki-radio>
    <ki-radio value="yearly">Yearly</ki-radio>
  </ki-radio-group>
  <ki-button variant="primary">Continue</ki-button>
</form>
```

A `disabled` group is skipped in Tab order and contributes no form entry; do not use it for pending or loading semantics:

```html

  <ki-radio value="eu">Europe</ki-radio>
  <ki-radio value="us">United States</ki-radio>
</ki-radio-group>

A bounded scroll container that clips its content along one declared axis
and replaces platform scrollbar chrome with a token-resolved indicator.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
a bounded region inside a view whose content can outgrow it:
chat or message panes, code and log blocks, tag rows, sidebar navigation,
tall menus inside cards. Give it bounds (its size comes entirely from your
layout) and a `label` (required: the accessible name of the scroll
region). Scrolling stays native — wheel, touch, keyboard and indicator
drag operate the viewport directly.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
page-level scrolling (the browser's job), carousels or
paginated media (future indicator/carousel patterns), virtualized long
collections, multi-column tabular data, or nesting scrollers (v1
guarantees a single scroll axis per region). Cross-axis overflow is an
authoring mistake: the scroller scrolls its declared axis only and clips
the other — wrap or size content on the cross axis.

Indicator fixes and token updates.

February

Initial scroller release.

 ``` `orientation="horizontal"` scrolls the inline axis instead; one axis per instance — the cross axis clips, so wrap or size content on it: ```html
MonTueWedThuFri
``` Scrolling stays native (wheel, touch, arrows, Page Up/Down, Home/End); the viewport joins the Tab order only while content actually overflows, and slotted content keeps its own semantics: ```html

 ```

whose slotted content keeps its own semantics (FR-006). Documented as
required: a scroller without a label renders but exposes no accessible
name and fails the accessibility audit (015-ki-progress precedent).
The label is never rendered visually.

props.name: orientation
props.docs:
Declared scroll axis, mapping the design source's `Type` axis:
`vertical` (default) scrolls the block axis, `horizontal` the inline
axis. One axis per instance; the cross axis clips. A structural axis,
never appearance — thickness, shape and colors of the indicator are
per-theme `--ki-scroller-*` tokens. An unrecognized value matches no
style selector and no `horizontal` code path, so the scroller keeps
the default vertical behavior (fallback by CSS construction plus a

# ki-segmented-control examples

## Change a chart range

```html
<ki-segmented-control id="range" label="Chart range" value="week">
  <ki-segment value="day">Day</ki-segment>
  <ki-segment value="week">Week</ki-segment>
  <ki-segment value="month">Month</ki-segment>
</ki-segmented-control>
```

```js
import { defineCustomElement as defineControl } from '@kimen/elements/ki-segmented-control';
import { defineCustomElement as defineSegment } from '@kimen/elements/ki-segment';

defineControl();
defineSegment();

document.querySelector('#range').addEventListener('ki-change', ({ detail }) => {
  updateChartRange(detail.value);
});
```

## Give an icon-only option a name

```html
<ki-segmented-control label="View" size="sm" full-width>
  <ki-segment value="list">List</ki-segment>
  <ki-segment value="board" aria-label="Board">
    <svg slot="start" viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true">
      <path d="M2 2h4v12H2zm6 0h6v7H8z" fill="currentColor"></path>
    </svg>
  </ki-segment>
</ki-segmented-control>
```

The all-elements loader already registers the tooltip. With direct imports
or framework wrappers, register it before mounting an icon-only option.

```js
import { defineCustomElement as defineTooltip } from '@kimen/elements/ki-tooltip';

defineTooltip();
```

accessible name and hover or focus tooltip from `aria-label`. Keep slotted
content noninteractive.

# Slider examples

Import the element and one theme stylesheet before mounting the examples.

```js
import '@kimen/tokens/css';
import { defineCustomElement } from '@kimen/elements/ki-slider';

defineCustomElement();
```

```html
<form>
  <ki-slider label="Volume" name="volume" help-text="Playback level"
    min="0" max="100" step="1" value="60" marks="5" format="percent"></ki-slider>
  <ki-slider label="Price per night" name="price" range
    value="20,80" format="currency" currency="EUR"></ki-slider>
  <button type="reset">Reset</button>
</form>

<ki-slider label="Exposure" centered min="-50" max="50" value="-20"></ki-slider>
<ki-slider label="Bass" orientation="vertical" max="10" value="4"></ki-slider>
```

A named slider contributes one form entry. The form above starts with
`volume=60` and `price=20,80`. Range values always run from lower to upper.
The closest `lang` controls the display format. Localize the thumb suffixes
through `minimum-label` and `maximum-label`.

```js
const volume = document.querySelector('ki-slider[name="volume"]');
volume.addEventListener('input', () => previewVolume(volume.value));
volume.addEventListener('change', () => saveVolume(volume.value));
```

The neutral catalog exposes the `change` action event. Bind it to a declared
action to receive the current value on commit.

# Stat

Use one stat for one key number. Choose the preference for the metric. Here,
the render time went down and the change is favorable.

```html
<ki-stat
  label="Median render time"
  value="84"
  unit="ms"
  delta="-9"
  delta-label="vs last week"
  direction="lower-is-better"
></ki-stat>
```

For a percentage comparison beside a count, set `deltaFormat` as a property.
Percent formatting takes a fraction, so 0.12 reads as 12%.

```html
<ki-stat id="active-surfaces" label="Active surfaces" value="1284" delta="0.12" delta-label="vs last week"></ki-stat>
```

```js
document.querySelector('#active-surfaces').deltaFormat = { style: 'percent' };
```

With no `delta`, the card shows the current value alone. For a trend that carries
no judgment, use `direction="neutral"`. For an informative sparkline, give the
chart a text equivalent through its own HTML semantics.

```html
<ki-stat label="Sales" value="750">
  <svg slot="chart" role="img" aria-label="Sales rose from 680 to 750 this week" viewBox="0 0 80 20" width="80" height="20">
    <path d="M1 17 L13 11 L27 14 L39 4 L52 8 L67 5 L79 1" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"></path>
  </svg>
</ki-stat>
```

Accessible name for the state ("Online", "Build failing"). With a

usage.examples:
# Table examples Wrap one native table and keep the caption, column scope and row scope in the markup. A selected row's `data-key` identifies its record after sorting or replacement. ```html
Services
Name Status Runs
Billing API Ready 64
Search index Slow 18
``` With individual imports or a framework wrapper, register `ki-checkbox` when using `selectable`. The full Kimen loader registers both elements. ```js import { defineCustomElement as defineTable } from '@kimen/elements/ki-table'; import { defineCustomElement as defineCheckbox } from '@kimen/elements/ki-checkbox'; defineTable(); defineCheckbox(); ``` Apply sort requests and update the native header state from the page. ```js const frame = document.querySelector('#services'); const table = frame.querySelector('table'); frame.addEventListener('ki-sort', ({ detail: { key, direction } }) => { if (key !== 'name') return; const body = table.tBodies[0]; const nameOf = (row) => row.querySelector('th[scope="row"]').textContent.trim(); const sign = direction === 'ascending' ? 1 : -1; body.append(...Array.from(body.rows).sort((a, b) => sign * nameOf(a).localeCompare(nameOf(b)))); for (const header of table.tHead.querySelectorAll('th[data-sort]')) { if (header.dataset.sort === key) header.setAttribute('aria-sort', direction); else header.removeAttribute('aria-sort'); } }); frame.addEventListener('ki-selection-change', ({ detail: { keys } }) => { updateBulkActions(keys); }); ``` Use `density="compact"` where the available block space is tight. During a refresh, set `loading` to mark the native table busy and show a placeholder below the existing records. Remove it once the refresh ends. For a person column, place `` next to the visible name. For a row menu, use a trailing "Actions" header and a button whose name includes the row. Import `@kimen/elements/icons/ellipsis` before mounting the glyph. ```html View service ``` Give each row trigger a unique ID and handle the menu's `ki-select` event in the application. Translate the checkbox labels with `select-all-label="Sélectionner toutes les lignes"` and `row-selection-label="Sélectionner {row}"` on a French page.

A token-styled multiline text field with native form semantics.

Like a native field, it answers `checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()`,
`setCustomValidity(message)`, `validity`, `validationMessage` and
`willValidate` synchronously, on the custom-elements build (not on hosts
created by the lazy loader).

descriptions, messages, delivery notes, or addresses when paired with a
matching `autocomplete` purpose.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
single-line values (`ki-input`), constrained choices,
rich or formatted text editing, or search boxes.

Agent note: initial text is declared through the `value` attribute; element
text content is ignored. Enter inserts a line break and never submits the
enclosing form, the inverse of `ki-input`.

after the person answered or submitted; a polite live region, starting with a

docsTags.name: event
docsTags.text:
change - Fired when the user commits an edited value (on blur, with native
textarea timing), composed across the shadow boundary; `value` is already
current when listeners run. When to use: react to a committed value. When
NOT to use: do not use it for per-keystroke updates; the native `input`
event carries those.

usage.examples:
A labeled multiline field in a form (`label` is mandatory — the visible label and accessible name); `rows` sets the stable visible line count (default `2`, no auto-grow in v1):

```html
<form>
  <ki-textarea label="Comments" name="comments" rows="4"></ki-textarea>
  <ki-button variant="primary">Send</ki-button>
</form>
```

Initial text is declared through the `value` attribute — element text content is ignored — and Enter inserts a line break, never submitting the enclosing form:

```html
<ki-textarea label="Bio" name="bio" value="Web components enthusiast."></ki-textarea>
```

`required` blocks submission while empty, and an `autocomplete` purpose such as `street-address` exposes the entry's meaning to autofill:

```html
<ki-textarea
  label="Shipping address"
  name="address"
  rows="3"
  autocomplete="street-address"
  required
></ki-textarea>
```

Read-only and disabled are distinct states — `readonly` stays focusable, selectable, submitted and validation-exempt; `disabled` is none of those:

```html
<ki-textarea label="Accepted policy" value="Version 2.1, accepted 2026-05-02." readonly></ki-textarea>
<ki-textarea label="Legacy notes" value="Migrated from v1." disabled></ki-textarea>
```

components.docs:
A short, transient message about something the person just did, shown
without blocking the page. It leaves on its own after its time, which stops
while the person points at the toaster, works inside it or is away from the
page; a toast with an action, or reporting an error, waits for the person.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
confirm an action that happened elsewhere on screen ("Changes
saved", "Link copied"), report a background result ("Export ready"), or
offer a quick undo. Raise it into a `ki-toaster`, in markup or with its
`show()` method; express urgency with `tone`.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
anything the person must read or act on to continue belongs
to `ki-dialog`; form validation belongs to the field's error text; a lasting
condition of the page belongs to `ki-alert`, which stays inline.

Assistive technology note: a toast announces as it appears, so append it
when the event happens; a toast present at initial page load is exposed with
its role but its announcement is not guaranteed. The heading and the message
are the whole announcement: the icon, the action and the dismiss button
stay outside the live region.

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text: - Message text. It lives inside the live-region boundary.

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text:
action - At most one action, as a `ki-button size="sm" variant="ghost"`.
Its own click handler runs, then the toast leaves (`reason: "action"`). A
toast holding an action never leaves on its own. When NOT to use: a response
the person cannot skip belongs in `ki-dialog`.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text:
toast - The flat surface: fill, image, edge, radius, padding,
elevation and backdrop filter.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: icon - The tone icon, drawn by the component in the tone's ink.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: heading - Optional bold first line, rendered only when non-empty.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: message - Message wrapper around the default slot.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: action - Wrapper around the `action` slot, rendered only when it holds content.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: dismiss - The dismiss `ki-icon-button`, rendered only when `dismissible`.

usage.examples:
Put a toast in a `ki-toaster` when something happens; it announces itself as it appears and leaves on its own after 5 seconds. `tone` picks the icon and its ink and the live-region urgency: `danger` exposes `role="alert"`, every other value `role="status"`:

```html
<ki-toaster>
  <ki-toast tone="success" heading="Changes saved">Workspace settings are up to date.</ki-toast>
</ki-toaster>
```

`duration` (milliseconds) changes the time; `0` keeps the toast until it is dismissed. A toast in the `danger` tone, or holding an action, never leaves on its own, whatever its `duration`. The time stops while the pointer rests on the toaster, while focus is inside it, or while the page is hidden:

```html
<ki-toast duration="8000">The export is ready in your downloads.</ki-toast>
<ki-toast tone="danger" heading="Upload failed">The file is larger than 20 MB.</ki-toast>
```

The `action` slot takes one ghost `ki-button size="sm"`. Its own click handler runs, then the toast leaves:

```html
<ki-toast heading="Message archived">
  The conversation moved to your archive.
  <ki-button slot="action" variant="ghost" size="sm">Undo</ki-button>
</ki-toast>
```

`ki-dismiss` says why the toast left: `detail.reason` is `"timeout"`, `"button"`, `"escape"` or `"action"`. `dismissible="false"` drops the dismiss button (Escape still works on a focused toast); `dismiss-label` is the component's only built-in word, so localize it whenever the document language is not English:

```html
<ki-toast lang="es" dismiss-label="Descartar">Borrador guardado.</ki-toast>
```

props.name: dismissLabel
props.docs:
Accessible name of the dismiss button. Override for localization; the
default English word is the component's only built-in text.

When to use: whenever the document language is not English.
When NOT to use: do not put the message here; use the default slot.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: 'Dismiss'

props.name: dismissed
props.docs:
Reflected state: true once the toast has left. The timer, the dismiss
button, Escape and the action set it; the page may set or clear it.
While true the host stays in the document but renders nothing and leaves
the accessibility tree. Clearing it shows the toast again with its full
time.

When to use: show a toast again, or close it from the page.
When NOT to use: do not read programmatic changes as dismissals;
`ki-dismiss` reports only the timer and the person.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: false

props.name: dismissible
props.docs:
Shows the dismiss button, a ghost `ki-icon-button` named by
`dismiss-label`. Escape still dismisses a focused toast without it.

When to use: keep it on unless the toast leaves on its own and the page
offers no other way to read it again.
When NOT to use: do not turn it off on a toast that waits for the person.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: true

props.name: duration
props.docs:
How long the toast stays, in milliseconds, before it leaves on its own;
`0` keeps it until it is dismissed. Ignored (treated as `0`) when the toast
holds an action or its tone is `danger`. Unset, or not a finite number of
zero or more, it is 5000. The time stops while the pointer rests on the
toaster, while focus is inside it, or while the page is hidden, and
continues with what was left. Changing it restarts the time.

When to use: give a longer message more time.
When NOT to use: do not shorten it below what a person needs to read the
message.

props.name: heading
props.docs:
Optional bold first line, inside the live region. Empty strings render no
heading. It is a `strong` element, never a document heading.

When to use: a short label for the event ("Changes saved").
When NOT to use: do not use it for page structure.

props.name: queued
props.docs:
Output-only state written by an enclosing `ki-toaster`: true while the
toast waits for a place. A queued toast renders nothing, is absent from
the accessibility tree and its time does not run. Authors do not set it;
the toaster overwrites it.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: false

props.name: tone
props.docs:
Picks the icon and its ink, and the live-region urgency: `danger` exposes
`role="alert"` and never leaves on its own; `neutral`, `info`, `success`,
`warning`, absent and unrecognized values expose `role="status"`. The
surface and the text look the same in every tone. Unknown values render
neutral.

When to use: choose the tone that describes what happened.
When NOT to use: do not use tone for emphasis; a lasting failure belongs
in `ki-alert`.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: 'neutral'

events.docs:
Fired once when the toast leaves because its time ran out
(`reason: "timeout"`), the person used the dismiss button (`"button"`),
pressed Escape inside it (`"escape"`) or activated its action
(`"action"`), after it is hidden and focus has been handed on. Not
cancelable. When to use: remove the element, or record that the message
was seen. When NOT to use: do not expect it for programmatic `dismissed`
changes.

slots.docs: Message text. It lives inside the live-region boundary.

slots.name: action
slots.docs:
At most one action, as a `ki-button size="sm" variant="ghost"`.
Its own click handler runs, then the toast leaves (`reason: "action"`). A
toast holding an action never leaves on its own. When NOT to use: a response
the person cannot skip belongs in `ki-dialog`.

parts.name: action
parts.docs: Wrapper around the `action` slot, rendered only when it holds content.

parts.name: dismiss
parts.docs: The dismiss `ki-icon-button`, rendered only when `dismissible`.

parts.name: heading
parts.docs: Optional bold first line, rendered only when non-empty.

parts.name: icon
parts.docs: The tone icon, drawn by the component in the tone's ink.

parts.name: message
parts.docs: Message wrapper around the default slot.

parts.name: toast
parts.docs:
The flat surface: fill, image, edge, radius, padding,
elevation and backdrop filter.

components.docs:
The one place toasts appear: it paints its `ki-toast` children in the top
layer at a corner of the viewport, stacks them in arrival order, shows the
newest few and queues the older ones, without covering the page beside
them.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
once per page (or once inside a modal `ki-dialog`), as the place
every `ki-toast` of the application appears in: append toasts to it, or call
`show()`. Choose the corner with `placement`.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
do not put anything but `ki-toast` elements in it; do not use
it for persistent content, which belongs in the page or in `ki-alert`.

Assistive technology note: while it shows toasts the toaster is a group
named by `label`, never a landmark; F6 moves focus into it and Escape on a
toast returns focus to where it was. An empty toaster exposes nothing and
covers nothing.

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text:
- The `ki-toast` elements, in arrival order. Other children are not
counted, queued or placed.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text:
stack - The stack in the top layer: placement, edge distance, gap
between toasts and width.

usage.examples:
Place one toaster per page (or one inside a modal `ki-dialog`). It paints its stack in the top layer, stacks toasts from the top down in arrival order and shows the newest three; older ones wait their turn:

```html
<ki-toaster></ki-toaster>
<script>
  document.querySelector('ki-toaster').show({
    tone: 'success',
    title: 'Changes saved',
    message: 'Workspace settings are up to date.',
    action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: undo },
  });
</script>
```

`show()` creates the toast, appends it, and removes it once it has left; its action renders as a ghost `ki-button size="sm"`. The toaster does not bundle either element, so define `ki-toast` and `ki-button` too. Toasts can also be written in markup inside the toaster; those stay the page's own and are never removed.

`placement` picks the corner — `top-center`, `top-end`, `bottom-center` or `bottom-end` (the default); `end` follows the writing direction, and a narrow touch screen always uses the bottom center. `max` sets how many toasts show at once:

```html
<ki-toaster placement="top-center" max="2"></ki-toaster>
```

While it shows toasts the toaster is a group named by `label` (`Notifications` by default); F6 moves focus into it, and Escape on a toast returns focus to where it was. Localize the name whenever the document language is not English:

```html
<ki-toaster lang="es" label="Avisos"></ki-toaster>
```

The distance from the viewport edges and the gap between toasts are tokens:

```css
:root {
  --ki-toaster-inset-block: 24px;
  --ki-toaster-inset-inline: 24px;
}
```

props.name: label
props.docs:
Accessible name of the group the toaster exposes while it shows toasts.
Override for localization.

When to use: provide the name in the document language.
When NOT to use: do not put a message here.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: 'Notifications'

props.name: max
props.docs:
How many toasts show at once: the newest ones. Older toasts wait, and come
back with their full time as shown ones leave. A toast holding focus keeps
its place until focus leaves the toaster; the oldest other one waits
instead. A value below 1 or not a whole number shows 3.

When to use: lower it on small screens or busy applications.
When NOT to use: do not raise it to show every toast; a tall stack covers
the page.

props.name: placement
props.docs:
Corner or edge of the viewport the stack sits against; `end` follows the
writing direction. On a coarse pointer and a viewport narrower than 40rem
the stack always sits at the bottom center. Unknown values place the stack
at the bottom end.

When to use: keep toasts away from where the page's own controls live.
When NOT to use: do not change it per toast; one toaster keeps one place.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: 'bottom-end'

methods.name: show
methods.docs:
Raises a toast: creates a `ki-toast` from `tone`, `title` (its heading),
`message`, `duration`, `dismissible` and `action` (a ghost
`ki-button size="sm"` in its `action` slot that calls `onClick`), appends
it to the toaster and resolves with it. Once the toast has left it is
removed from the page. The toaster does not bundle `ki-toast` or
`ki-button`: define them, as for toasts written in markup.
When to use: raise a toast from script without writing its markup.
When NOT to use: a toast written in markup stays the page's own: append
it instead, and it is never removed.

slots.docs:
The `ki-toast` elements, in arrival order. Other children are not
counted, queued or placed.

parts.name: stack
parts.docs:
The stack in the top layer: placement, edge distance, gap
between toasts and width.

components.docs: A transient, text-only description bubble for one slotted trigger.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
add a brief clarifying hint for an icon-only, abbreviated, or
otherwise ambiguous control when the same information is discoverable
elsewhere in the interface.

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
essential or unique information in a tooltip; interactive
or rich content in a tooltip; form validation messages, disabled controls,
or touch-primary flows. Use visible layout text or a future `ki-popover`
pattern for those cases.

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text:
- Exactly one interactive trigger. The component reflects `label` to
the trigger's `aria-description`.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: tooltip - The non-focusable tooltip bubble.

usage.examples:
`label` is the entire tooltip content, reflected to the slotted trigger's accessible description; the trigger must already carry its own accessible name:

```html
<ki-tooltip label="Copies a shareable link to the clipboard">
  <ki-button type="button">Copy link</ki-button>
</ki-tooltip>
```

`placement` (default `top`; also `bottom`, `start`, `end`) is a preference — the component flips or clamps it to keep the bubble inside the viewport:

```html
<ki-tooltip label="Downloads the report as PDF" placement="bottom">
  <ki-button type="button">Export</ki-button>
</ki-tooltip>
```

An empty or whitespace-only `label` renders no tooltip and exposes no description — useful for conditional hints; never put essential or unique information in a tooltip:

```html
<ki-tooltip label="">
  <ki-button type="button">No hint here</ki-button>
</ki-tooltip>
```

props.name: label
props.docs:
The entire tooltip content. The string is reflected to the slotted
trigger's accessible description without changing its name. Empty or
whitespace-only labels render no tooltip and expose no description.
When to use: a short hint that clarifies the slotted trigger.
When NOT to use: never use `label` for essential information, rich
content, interactive content, validation messages, or information attached
to disabled controls; put that content in visible UI or a future popover.

props.name: placement
props.docs:
Preferred placement for the tooltip. The component may flip or clamp the
rendered placement to keep the bubble inside the viewport; unknown runtime
values fall back to `top`.
When NOT to use: do not depend on placement for meaning or reading order.

docsTags.name: default
docsTags.text: 'top'

Exactly one interactive trigger. The component reflects `label` to
the trigger's `aria-description`.

parts.name: tooltip
parts.docs: The non-focusable tooltip bubble.

components.docs:
A themed video surface: a calm poster facade with exactly one accessible
play control over a slotted native `<video>` element. From the first
activation on, playback, scrubbing, volume, captions and fullscreen belong
to the native player — Kimen ships no custom chrome.

docsTags.name: whenToUse
docsTags.text:
playable content the person deliberately chooses to watch —
product tours, talks, tutorials, announcements — presented as a poster
with one play control. Slot exactly one native `<video>` carrying its own
`poster`, sources and `<track>` captions, omit `controls` (the component
enables the native chrome the moment the facade yields, FR-002), and give
the control a `label` (required: the accessible name of the play button).

docsTags.name: whenNotToUse
docsTags.text:
decorative background or ambient loops (plain CSS and
`<video>` are the tool), audio-only content (a future audio component),
embeds from streaming platforms that ship their own player chrome (use
their embed), or static imagery (use an image, not a video). `autoplay`
on the slotted media is unsupported: the facade's contract is that
playback begins only by explicit user activation — never on scroll,
hover or visibility — so preexisting `autoplay` and `controls` on the
slotted media are cleared when it arrives, and any playback already
running is paused (FR-003; the native chrome returns at activation).

docsTags.name: slot
docsTags.text: - Exactly one native `<video>` element carrying its own poster, sources and `<track>` captions.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: frame - The media frame: radius, clipping, the themed surface.

docsTags.name: part
docsTags.text: play - The play control: overlay scrim, glass container and glyph.

usage.examples:
Slot exactly one native `<video>` carrying its own poster, sources and `<track>` captions; `label` names the play control (required — never rendered visually) and the native chrome returns the moment the facade yields:

```html
<ki-video label="Play the product tour">
  <video muted playsinline width="1280" height="720" poster="tour.jpg">
    <source src="tour.webm" type="video/webm" />
    <track kind="captions" srclang="en" label="English" src="tour.en.vtt" />
  </video>
</ki-video>
```

Everything on the media element passes through untouched — offer format fallbacks through multiple `<source>` children, and the native media events (`play`, `pause`, `ended`) keep firing on the element you own; ki-video emits no events of its own:

```html
<ki-video label="Play the setup walkthrough">
  <video width="1280" height="720" poster="walkthrough.jpg">
    <source src="walkthrough.webm" type="video/webm" />
    <source src="walkthrough.mp4" type="video/mp4" />
    <track kind="captions" srclang="en" label="English" src="walkthrough.en.vtt" />
  </video>
</ki-video>
```

The frame fills its container's inline size and the media keeps the intrinsic aspect ratio declared by `width`/`height` (16:9 is a demonstration, not a constraint); `autoplay` and `controls` on arriving media are cleared — playback begins only from the play control:

```html
<ki-video label="Play the workshop recording">
  <video width="800" height="600" poster="workshop.jpg">
    <source src="workshop.mp4" type="video/mp4" />
    <track kind="captions" srclang="en" label="English" src="workshop.en.vtt" />
  </video>
</ki-video>
```

props.name: label
props.docs:
Accessible name of the play control ("Play the product tour"). The
control is a real button exposing role button with exactly this name;
the frame contributes no role, name or state of its own (FR-004,
FR-005). Documented as required: no default human-language string is
baked in, and an unlabeled control renders but fails the accessibility
audit (015-ki-progress precedent). The label is never rendered visually.
